title: Layer annotations fail to be pushed to remote registry on first attempt
body:
Moving from https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/27796 as suggested in [this comment](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/27796#issuecomment-5486886986) since apparently the issue is in container-libs rather than podman.

### Description

When pushing an image with layer annotations to a remote OCI registry, the layer annotations aren't pushed to the remote registry unless the layer is already present. As a result, pushing the image a *second* time results in the layer annotations being uploaded.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Generate an image that has layer annotations. To test this, I used [chunkah](https://github.com/coreos/chunkah) to rechunk `quay.io/fedora/fedora-iot:44`, producing an image with an `"org.chunkah.component"` annotation on each layer.
2. Run `skopeo inspect containers-storage:...` to confirm that the local image has layer annotations as expected.
3. Push the image to a remote registry (e.g. with `podman push`).
4. Run `skopeo inspect docker://...` and observe that the remote copy of the image is missing layer annotations.
5. Push the same image to the remote registry a second time.
6. Run the same `skopeo inspect docker://...` command a second time and observe that the layer annotations are now present.

You can see the results of these steps on a GitHub Actions Ubuntu 26.04 runner here: https://github.com/HastD/scratchwork/actions/runs/33510058256/job/99863284785

Here are the raw logs from the above run:  [logs_90801797984.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31693052/logs_90801797984.zip)

### Expected result

Layer annotations should be preserved when pushing to a remote registry.

### Actual result

Layer annotations are missing after pushing if the layer wasn't already present in the remote registry.

### Discussion

@TheMDev might have found the cause of the issue here: https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/27796#issuecomment-5486886986 (I'm not familiar enough with this codebase to evaluate the accuracy of that comment, but it looks plausible)

comments.body:
Thanks for your report.

Yes, this is the right repo, and that comment is correct at least as far as pointing at the FIXME comment goes.
